newsitem.title: GERMANY: Italy's Prodi says talked accounts with Kohl.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says talked accounts with Kohl.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Friday he had discussed elements of public accounts policies in his meeting with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl but did not focus on the possibility of Italy bringing forward the bill for its 1998 budget.

"We talked about public accounts but we did not specifically talk about bringing forward the 1998 budget bill. Rather, we illustrated to each other all of the details of our policies," he told a news briefing for Italian journalists.
Prodi noted however that a move to bring forward its budget could be of clear use in signalling Italy's economic plans to financial operators.
"It could be useful to them to have a longer span of time and know by the end of summer what the 1998 budget bill will be like," he said.
He said the pensions would be an important part of Italy's future policies but that a programme on pensions could not be undertaken without "broad consultation with the entire country".

Referring to Thursday's meeting between Kohl and Italian PDS party leader Massimo D'Alemo, Prodi scotched suggestions that the discussions had in anyway pre-empted his meeting with the German Chancellor, saying that he was fully aware of the meeting.
